A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RobustSpring study. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching reorganized material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 16 model configurations, subsampling and ranking analyses, rain/snow masking experiments, and a KITTI noise-transfer experiment.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results, adds SEA-RAFT evaluations, and reports original disparity-validation and human perceptual-study results.

M1.justification: The corruption-generation procedures and parameters, clean-versus-corrupted prediction metric, subsampling, and ranking procedures are retained. Expanded consistency and robustness explanations do not establish an algorithmic change; SEA-RAFT is an added evaluated model.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds a human perceptual-selection task using five corruption types at three severities. The main Spring benchmark retains the same three dense-matching tasks and 20 corruptions, and the KITTI noise-transfer scenario already appeared in v1.

E2.justification: SEA-RAFT joins the optical-flow benchmark and corresponding subsampling, ranking, and corruption-group comparisons, increasing optical-flow methods from eight to nine. The existing optical-flow, scene-flow, and stereo comparator configurations remain.

E3.justification: New validation protocols include MS-RAFT+ disparity evaluation on the Spring validation set and 140 perceptual comparisons with randomly ordered alternatives at SSIM 0.95, 0.7, and 0.2. Existing benchmark metrics, corruption settings, subsampling, and KITTI selection procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.5–A.6 add previously absent checks of two central dataset-design choices: estimated geometry and corruption severity. v2 also adds quadratic fits to accuracy-versus-robustness plots. The earlier subsampling, corruption-group, rain/snow masking, and KITTI transfer analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 adds standard-deviation rows to the optical-flow, scene-flow, and stereo tables. These describe dispersion across corruption types, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports benchmark seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing models' main benchmark scores are unchanged, but SEA-RAFT adds substantial results: mean corruption EPE 2.96 and median 1.20, versus v1's leading GMFlow mean 2.98 and GMA median 1.39. v2 also reports disparity EPE 1.09 pixels, D1-all 5.60%, and perceptual agreement 87.14%. The Schulze matrix entries are revised as well as expanded.

T1.justification: The metric and corruption equations, including Eqs. 1–18, and the ranking mathematics are retained. The new discussion of projected motion, prediction stability, and perfect accuracy is conceptual clarification, without a new formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The central dataset and metric contributions remain. The contribution list expands the evaluation from 16 to 17 model configurations and changes website integration from something that 'can be integrated' to something that 'is integrated'; Appendix A.8 nevertheless describes its illustrations as mock-ups.

C2.justification: v2 substantially clarifies applicability: robustness measures stability rather than accuracy, a perfectly accurate model can score poorly when corruptions alter motion, and rain/snow may be meaningful content in some applications. It also expands explanations of noise-versus-weather behavior, omitted corruption families, and limitations of extrinsics validation.

D1.justification: v2 adds GPU and CPU specifications, inference and server-evaluation times, SEA-RAFT's repository and checkpoint, and exact KITTI frame identifiers with noise estimates. It also describes raw versus curated data provision. Conversely, v1's explicit CC BY 4.0 license and submission-quota statements are removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including SEA-RAFT, Horn–Schunck, and Bauer et al.'s generalization study, while removing FlowBench, DispBench, and the synthetic-versus-real corruption study. Related work broadens 'first robustness benchmark for three dense-matching tasks' to 'first dense-matching robustness benchmark,' although most positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose remain. v2 rewrites portions of the results discussion, expands explanatory passages, moves references before a consolidated appendix, and updates authorship and affiliations. Existing supplementary methods and analyses remain identifiable within the reorganized appendix.

P2.justification: v2 switches from two-column formatting to a single-column conference layout and extensively reorganizes displays. It combines the corruption overview with its consistency table, merges scene-flow/stereo and metric tables into paired panels, groups existing plots, and adds regression curves, perceptual-study examples, and website mock-ups.

improvement.justification: The geometry and perceptual checks in Appendices A.5–A.6, clearer metric limitations, and added reproducibility information provide a limited net improvement. Reporting problems constrain the gain: Section 4.1 still names GMA as median winner despite SEA-RAFT's better table score, Table 5 misaligns method labels, and the Spring-labelled SEA-RAFT checkpoint leaves the blanket no-Spring-finetuning claim unclear.
